cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is a prisoner on a ship headed for Italy, and a storm has been shoving that ship around for two weeks. It's the fourteenth night, they're still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, and the man writing this book is on board with them. Then, about midnight, the sailors start to sense something.

cards.question: About midnight on the fourteenth night, what do the sailors sense the ship is getting close to?

cards.text: So they drop a weighted line to check how deep the water is. Twenty fathoms. They go a little farther and check AGAIN.

cards.question: After a reading of twenty fathoms, the sailors go a little farther, and the next sounding reads ___ fathoms.

cards.text: Shallower water in the middle of the night, and they're scared of running aground on the rocks, so down go four anchors from the stern. It's that midnight walk across a dark kitchen when you KNOW you left a cookie sheet on the floor somewhere.

cards.question: With four anchors down from the stern, the sailors pray for daybreak.

cards.text: Meanwhile, some of the sailors get real busy up at the bow. They act like they're lowering more anchors from the front of the ship.

cards.question: Instead of anchors, what are the sailors at the bow really letting down into the sea?
The sailors lowering the lifeboat are trying to escape from the ship.

cards.text: Paul catches on, and friend, two weeks in a storm as a PRISONER and this man is STILL on top of it. He goes straight to the centurion, the Roman officer in charge of the prisoners, and the soldiers.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the centurion and the soldiers about the sailors in the lifeboat?

answers.text: If they leave you cannot be saved
Let them go so the ship is lighter
Lock them below deck until morning

cards.text: So the soldiers cut the ropes and let the lifeboat drift away. No lifeboat, no backup plan, NO EXIT, and me? I'd have been hanging onto that rope yelling, "Hold on, can we TALK about this?"
Right up to daybreak, Paul keeps working on everybody about one thing. He tells them, "Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food."

cards.question: Right up to daybreak, Paul keeps urging everyone on board to ___.
Paul tells the men that not a single hair of their heads will be lost.

cards.text: Then Paul takes bread and gives thanks to God in front of them all. He breaks it and starts eating, right there in the middle of all that suspense.

cards.question: Watching Paul eat, the rest of the men on board stay too afraid to touch any food.

cards.text: In all, there are 276 people on board, and it's just like the box of cookies at a work meeting: NOBODY touches it until one brave person goes first. Then? Gone. Crumbs. Empty box. In four minutes.

cards.question: Once everyone on board has eaten their fill, how do they lighten the ship?

answers.text: Throw the grain into the sea

cards.text: When daylight finally comes, nobody recognizes the land. But they spot a bay with a sandy beach.

cards.question: What do they decide to do at that bay with the sandy beach?

cards.text: They cut away the anchors, loosen the ropes on the rudders and hoist the foresail to the wind. Here we go, friend, straight for the beach.

cards.question: The ship makes it all the way onto the sandy beach.

cards.text: The ship hits a sandbar and runs aground. The bow is stuck fast and won't move, and the stern is getting broken up by the waves, like a cookie glued to the pan on one end and crumbling on the other.

cards.question: With the ship breaking up, the soldiers plan to kill the prisoners so none of them can ___ to freedom.

cards.text: Those prisoners include Paul. But the centurion steps in and shuts the whole plan down.

cards.question: Why does the centurion stop the soldiers' plan to kill the prisoners?

answers.text: He wants to spare Paul's life
He needs every prisoner for trial
He is afraid of the sailors

cards.question: The centurion orders those who can swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

cards.text: Everybody else follows on planks and pieces of the ship. And I don't care who you are, NOBODY looks cool paddling a piece of a ship.

cards.question: When it's all over, how many of the 276 people on board are brought safely to land?

cards.text: Soaking wet, on a beach nobody recognizes, but every one of them is standing on land. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this trip is NOT finished.

findings.problem: The card says Paul is a prisoner on a ship headed for Italy. That comes from Acts 27:1, which is outside this passage, but the card gives no reference for it and cites only Acts 27:27.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls the centurion the Roman officer in charge of the prisoners and calls Paul a PRISONER. Both facts come from Acts 27:1, outside this passage, but the card gives no reference and cites only Acts 27:31.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card says 'some of the sailors' get busy at the bow. Acts 27:30 says 'the sailors' attempted to escape. The card narrows the group in a way the text doesn't.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question calls them 'the sailors in the lifeboat.' Acts 27:30 says only that they let the lifeboat down into the sea, and Paul says 'Unless these men remain with the ship' (27:31). The text never puts the sailors in the lifeboat. The question could say 'the sailors lowering the lifeboat' instead.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This card's fact is the count of 276 people on board (Acts 27:37). Its joke is about nobody eating until one person goes first and then everyone eating. That is the action of Acts 27:35-36, not the fact on this card, so the comparison doesn't match the card's core action. The joke also suggests the men were waiting for someone to go first. Acts 27:36 gives the reason they ate: they 'were all encouraged.'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 18 already asks about Acts 27:44 and reveals that everyone reached land. This card repeats that answer ('every one of them is standing on land') before the line saying the story isn't over. That makes it a recap. Since the last verse is asked on a choice card, this card can be just the line saying the story isn't over.
